slice.observation: TensorFlow checkpoint loading matches values by traversing a directed object-dependency graph with named edges. restore queues requested restorations and applies values when a matching path becomes available; unmatched variables can be restored later when created. Saving recursively gathers reachable tracked objects, and supported list/dict wrappers participate in tracking and deferred restoration.
slice.inference: For TensorFlow checkpoints, nested update and restore propagation is path- and trackability-dependent rather than an unconditional eager invariant. The behavior depends on TensorFlow's recognized trackable graph and container semantics, so it must remain framework-scoped until another provider or framework is checked independently.
slice.scope_limit: single TensorFlow checkpoint primary-source leaf; no cross-provider generalization

continuation.exact_next_action: Fetch one current official TensorFlow primary source for tf.train.Checkpoint restore status/assertion semantics to distinguish restore lifecycle guarantees from object-graph propagation.
